learningObjective: Diagnose register-spill-induced slowdown from Nsight Compute metrics and compiler diagnostics.
stem: A custom CUDA kernel's Nsight Compute report and compiler output are shown. Which mitigation is most directly indicated?
profileData:
Compiler output (nvcc --ptxas-options=-v):
  ptxas info: Used 168 registers, 96 KB shared, 40 stack frame, 320 bytes spill stores, 480 bytes spill loads

Nsight Compute metrics:
  Achieved Occupancy: 0.12
  Warp Stall Reason (top): Long Scoreboard (memory latency)
  L1 Local Load Traffic: 22% of L1 traffic (unusually high; local memory is where spills go)
  DRAM Throughput: 30%
  SM Utilization: 40%

options.text: 40% SM utilization indicates the kernel is under-scheduled by the GPU driver; setting CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0 and using per-thread default streams will bring SM utilization to 100% and fix the underlying issue.

The 0.12 occupancy directly bounds SM throughput; raising `blockDim` (larger blocks) will proportionally increase performance because more threads per block always means more concurrent warps hiding latency.

Register spilling to local memory (evident from the 40-byte stack frame + 320/480 spill stores/loads and the abnormally high L1 local-load traffic) is causing costly memory traffic disguised as 'Long Scoreboard' stalls. Mitigations: reduce register usage via `__launch_bounds__` or `-maxrregcount`, refactor to fewer live variables, or restructure the algorithm to shrink working set.

The kernel is memory-bound at 30% DRAM throughput; the fix is to remove the shared-memory usage entirely because shared memory competes with registers for chip area, so shrinking shared memory automatically frees more registers per thread.

explanation: The compiler diagnostic shows explicit register spills (stack frame + spill stores/loads). Nsight Compute confirms unusual L1 local-load traffic — local memory (in CUDA terminology) is where spilled registers live. The 'Long Scoreboard' stall is caused by these spills going through L1/L2/DRAM. Reducing register usage (via `__launch_bounds__`, refactoring, or algorithmic changes) directly addresses the root cause. B, C, D fabricate mechanisms or misdiagnose.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING and default streams do not affect SM occupancy.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: raising blockDim doesn't fix per-thread register pressure.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: standard register-spill diagnosis and mitigation.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: shared memory and register file are separate hardware resources; removing shared memory does not free registers.

assumptions: The kernel was compiled with default optimization and the ptxas verbose output is accurate.
nonImplications: Does not imply `__launch_bounds__` always helps; it can force higher spills if the underlying algorithm needs many live values.
Does not imply spills are always fatal; small spills can be masked by warp scheduling.

distractorRationales.B: Confuses block size with register pressure.
distractorRationales.D: Confuses shared memory with register file.

sourceRefs.locator: Register pressure and local-memory traffic analysis
